vulnerabilities.name: Reentrancy
vulnerabilities.description: A callee can reenter a contract before its first invocation finishes.
vulnerabilities.root_cause: State is updated after an external call, allowing repeated use of stale state.

evidence.excerpt: An external contract can take over control flow and call back before the first function invocation finishes. Remediation: perform internal state changes before the external call, using checks-effects-interactions, or use a reentrancy lock. A lock blocks the unwanted callback into the protected path; it does not prevent control passing to the external callee.

vulnerabilities.name: Unchecked Call Return Value
vulnerabilities.description: A low-level call can fail while the caller continues as if it succeeded.
vulnerabilities.root_cause: The return value from the call is not checked.

evidence.excerpt: Low-level calls return a success value. A low-level call may fail and return false while the caller continues. Ignoring that return value can leave contract accounting inconsistent because the caller may record an operation as successful when the call failed.

vulnerabilities.name: Unprotected Ether Withdrawal
vulnerabilities.description: An unauthorized caller can withdraw funds when a withdrawal function lacks authorization.
vulnerabilities.root_cause: A sensitive withdrawal path omits access control.

evidence.excerpt: Missing access restrictions on functions that transfer ether can allow arbitrary users to withdraw funds. Implement controls so withdrawals can only be triggered by authorized parties. The source's sample access control checks msg.sender against a stored creator or owner and uses an onlyOwner modifier.

vulnerabilities.name: Unprotected SELFDESTRUCT
vulnerabilities.description: A caller may trigger contract destruction behavior if the operation is not protected.
vulnerabilities.root_cause: The sensitive selfdestruct operation lacks authorization.

evidence.excerpt: Unrestricted access to selfdestruct can let an unauthorized actor trigger destructive contract behavior.

vulnerabilities.name: Delegatecall to Untrusted Callee
vulnerabilities.description: Delegated code executes in the calling contract's context and may alter its storage.
vulnerabilities.root_cause: A contract delegates execution to an attacker-controlled address.

evidence.excerpt: Delegatecall runs callee code with the caller's storage and balance; untrusted callees can change caller state.

vulnerabilities.name: DoS with Failed Call
vulnerabilities.description: One reverting external call can block an operation for everyone.
vulnerabilities.root_cause: A batch or critical path depends on a recipient call succeeding.

evidence.excerpt: A failing external call can revert a wider transaction and prevent progress for other participants.

vulnerabilities.name: Transaction Order Dependence
vulnerabilities.description: A transaction's result can change based on another transaction's ordering.
vulnerabilities.root_cause: Contract logic assumes an unguaranteed order of pending transactions.

evidence.excerpt: Transactions visible before inclusion may be reordered, changing outcomes when logic depends on ordering.

vulnerabilities.name: Authorization through tx.origin
vulnerabilities.description: Using tx.origin for authorization can permit calls relayed through a malicious contract.
vulnerabilities.root_cause: Authorization checks the transaction origin rather than the immediate caller.

evidence.excerpt: tx.origin identifies the original transaction sender, not the immediate caller, so it is unsafe for authorization.

vulnerabilities.name: Block Timestamp Dependence
vulnerabilities.description: Timestamp-dependent logic may be influenced within permitted block production bounds.
vulnerabilities.root_cause: Security-critical behavior relies on a timestamp as an exact or unpredictable value.

evidence.excerpt: Block timestamps are not exact clocks and should not be relied upon for critical randomness or precision.

vulnerabilities.name: Weak Sources of Randomness
vulnerabilities.description: Predictable on-chain values cannot provide secure randomness for adversarial outcomes.
vulnerabilities.root_cause: Random outcomes depend on manipulable or observable block data.

evidence.excerpt: Blockchain attributes used as randomness can be observed or influenced and are unsuitable for secure random outcomes.

vulnerabilities.name: Integer Overflow and Underflow
vulnerabilities.description: Unchecked arithmetic in relevant compiler versions or unchecked blocks can wrap values.
vulnerabilities.root_cause: Arithmetic is performed without overflow checks in a context where wrapping is unsafe.

evidence.excerpt: Arithmetic overflow or underflow can produce unexpected values when checks are absent; compiler behavior varies by version.

vulnerabilities.name: Uninitialized Storage Pointer
vulnerabilities.description: An uninitialized storage reference can overwrite an unintended storage slot.
vulnerabilities.root_cause: A local storage pointer is declared without explicit initialization.

evidence.excerpt: Uninitialized storage pointers can reference unexpected storage locations and corrupt contract state.

vulnerabilities.name: Signature Malleability
vulnerabilities.description: Different valid signatures may represent the same signed message, defeating signature-byte uniqueness checks.
vulnerabilities.root_cause: Logic treats signature bytes as a unique identifier without normalization.

evidence.excerpt: ECDSA signatures can have multiple valid representations for the same message unless canonicalization is enforced.

vulnerabilities.name: Function Default Visibility
vulnerabilities.description: Older Solidity code may expose functions unintentionally when visibility is omitted.
vulnerabilities.root_cause: A function declaration relies on a compiler default instead of explicit visibility.

evidence.excerpt: Older Solidity versions allowed functions without explicit visibility, which could expose functions publicly.

vulnerabilities.name: Assert Violation
vulnerabilities.description: An invalid internal invariant can cause an assert failure and revert.
vulnerabilities.root_cause: Program logic permits a state that violates an asserted invariant.

evidence.excerpt: An assert failure indicates a violated internal invariant and causes the transaction to revert.

vulnerabilities.name: Price Oracle Manipulation
vulnerabilities.description: A contract can act on a distorted price when it relies on a manipulable oracle feed.
vulnerabilities.root_cause: Security-critical calculations trust an unvalidated or manipulable price source.

evidence.excerpt: Price oracle manipulation exploits weaknesses in price feeds to distort contract logic; validate inputs and use resilient oracle sources.
Aggregate multiple price sources. Use time-weighted averages (TWAPs) over sufficient windows to resist short-lived manipulations. Reject prices older than a maximum staleness threshold.
